text:
For most people, the **JBL Charge 6** is the best pool and beach speaker. It has an IP68 dust and water rating, about 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and strong sound for its size, and it costs around $130–150. Your choice mainly depends on whether you want to carry it in a beach bag or fill a party with sound.

| Pick | Best for | Key specs | Approx. price | Where to buy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **JBL Charge 6** | Best all-around | IP68, 20–28 hr battery, charges your phone | $130–160 | [What Hi-Fi's buy links](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) (Walmart $129.99, Amazon $149.95) · [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| **Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4** | Budget, small, floats | IP67, about 14 hr, 360° sound | ~$65 | [BestProducts' buy links](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) · [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| **JBL Grip** | Lightest to carry (0.85 lb) | IP68, 12 hr | ~$100 | [Good Housekeeping's buy links](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |
| **Ultimate Ears Epicboom** | 360° sound for groups around a pool | IP67, floats, about 15 hr | Mid-range | [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) · [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) |
| **JBL Boombox 4** | Big pool parties | Floats, 40+ hr battery, very loud | Premium | [RTINGS' buy links](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| **Soundcore Boom 2 Plus** | Loud boombox for less money | 100 W (140 W with BassUp), IPX7, floats, 20 hr | $249.99, or about $200 with code **AFSC20** | [Dealectric deal page](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus) |

**Notes on each pick:**
- **Charge 6:** What Hi-Fi named it the best waterproof speaker overall, and BestProducts and iTechGuides also picked it as their top choice. It has a higher water rating than most competitors. It doesn't float, so keep it out of the pool.
- **Wonderboom 4:** This is the easy pick if you want something small that survives a dunk and floats back up. It's not very loud and has no app.
- **Epicboom:** Tom's Guide and RTINGS both rank it highly. Its 360° design means it sounds the same from every side.
- **Boombox 4:** RTINGS's top waterproof pick. It's heavy and expensive, and it sounds muffled if you're behind it.
- **Boom 2 Plus:** This is a Dealectric deal page. Dealectric says it tested the code in Soundcore's cart on Oct 22, and the code expires Dec 31. It's an affiliate link, so they earn a commission. The speaker weighs 3.8 kg and has **no dust rating** (IPX7), so it's better for the pool than for sandy beaches.

**Tips for pool and beach use:**
- For sand, look for a rating starting with 6 (IP67 or IP68). An "X" rating like IPX7 means the speaker wasn't tested for dust.
- IP ratings don't cover salt water or chlorine. RTINGS recommends rinsing the speaker with fresh water after use.
- Keep the charging port sealed and let the speaker dry before charging.

My pick is the **JBL Charge 6** for most people. Get the **Wonderboom 4** if you're on a budget, and the **Boombox 4** if you're throwing a party.
